newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli panel re-affirms results of phone tender.
newsitem.headline: Israeli panel re-affirms results of phone tender.

text.p: Israel's Communications Ministry said on Sunday that its tenders committee had re-affirmed its two choices for the right to operate international telephone services.

"In a full investigation that was undertaken no irregularities were found, as had been earlier feared, in any decisions or calculations done by the tenders committee," the ministry said in a statement. "The indentities of the winners in the tenders remain as before, the Golden Lines and Barak groups."

The committee decided last week to re-examine the scoring system used to award the licences after Dolphin, one of the losing consortia, won a temporary Tel Aviv District Court order blocking granting of the licences. Dolphin claims that the committee scored the six bids incorrectly.
Dolphin comprises Bellsouth Corp, the Safra family, Israel's Discount Investment Corp, Israsat and Canada's Teleglobe.

Golden Lines and Barak won the tender in early November. Golden Lines comprises SBC Communications, Italy's STET and three Israeli partners. Barak includes Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and two Israeli companies -- Clalcom Ltd and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
The ministry said the committee did uncover a small mistake in the scoring between the two winning groups, but that it did not effect the outcome.
The tender entitles the licencees to offer overseas telephone service in competition with state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecom.
